analysis.title: GS TMT SPEC SALES: SpaceX shows AI demand is there; Elisa disappoints; Netflix guide; CTS Eventim gets an activist; IOS27 bites; DSY Frontier risk
key_insights: SpaceX (SPCX) rose about 8% after hours on a strong print. Q1 2027 revenue was guided to $33-37B against a Street figure of about $22B, and Q4 capex to $35-40B for an accelerated AI buildout.

About 93% of SpaceX's SI segment revenue (over $7.0B) came from compute sales and leasing. Cursor added a smaller piece and advertising added $0.5B. SI is now larger than Starlink and just over half of total SpaceX revenue, with payback under 1 year and a $63B backlog.

SpaceX raised its 2027 compute capacity target from about 10 GW to at least 13 GW, and the upside case from about 15 GW to over 20 GW. Current capacity is 1.7 GW, with 2.5-3.0 GW targeted by end-2026. The desk notes many have been sceptical of the 13 GW target.

Terrafab is targeting a first functional test chip (likely SRAM) at its Austin lab in May or June next year, and volume production at Gibbons Creek around Q3 2028. Musk called the timelines very aggressive. Musk also confirmed special committees are exploring a Tesla merger, which he called a good idea.

Bulls see the cleanest AI-segment ramp yet at SpaceX. Bears focus on another step-up in capex and deeply negative 9M free cash flow, a 'spend now, monetize later' pattern. Meta reports tonight as the first live test of whether a hyperscaler holds 2026/27 capex while FCF is under pressure.
Business Insider reports Amazon's internal commentary confirms power constraints are already forcing idle racks and multi-year FCF negativity.

Netflix fell about 5-6% overnight on a softer Q4 outlook and a reduced 2026 advertising outlook, despite Q3 results beating the Street and GS forecasts. Management still expects durable double-digit revenue growth. GIR says Q4 guidance could prove conservative. The desk notes NFLX is retesting its YTD low.

Elisa disappointed in Q3: revenue -0.2% vs consensus, mobile service revenue (MSR) -2.3%, EBITDA -1.5% miss, EBIT -4.9% miss, capex 14% above consensus. Mobile churn rose to 18.7% from 16.7% in Q2. FY26 guidance was reiterated and looks challenging given the MSR miss.

Activist Ananym Capital took an undisclosed stake in CTS Eventim. It sees 50-100% upside from self-help: buybacks, better transparency, stable management and using AI to improve the customer experience. Shares are down nearly 50% from peak and trade at a 44% discount to Live Nation.

Apple's iOS 27 WebKit changes block signals used by identity-resolution providers such as The Trade Desk and LiveRamp. GS sees this as negative for the open-web ad ecosystem and a relative positive for logged-in platforms (Meta, Google, Amazon). The eventual impact depends on adtech workarounds, iOS 27 adoption speed and any extension to macOS.

OpenAI acquired Orchestra Bio and is integrating it into its Rosalind AI suite for life sciences. The desk flags this as negative for Veeva and a further long-term competitor for Dassault Systemes (DSY) and its BIOVIA Scientific AI. Veeva dipped but ended flat.
Trendforce expects 4Q DRAM contract prices to rise about 20% qoq, slowing from about 80% in 2Q and 40% in 3Q.

Terafab reportedly approached about 10 Korean semiconductor suppliers at SEMICON West. The desk reads this as supporting a broader KOSDAQ equipment and materials thesis rather than a narrow large-cap Korea trade.

Tele2 capex commentary was reassuring: only SEK50-75m of hardware spend slips into 2027, so the 2026 capex cut looks largely structural and could add a low-single-digit uplift to FCF. Leverage is 1.5x and positioning may be short.

Stride (Pearson's virtual schools competitor) reported Q1 FY27 revenue of $639mn, up 3% y/y and 4% above consensus, but enrolments fell 2.5% vs consensus -0.6%. GS sees a slightly positive read-across for Pearson, which reports 22 October. GS expects Pearson Q3 organic growth of 5.4% vs consensus 5.5%.

US trading desk: equities stabilised through the afternoon with RTY > SPX > NDX. About 400 S&P names finished up. Floor activity was 4 out of 10. Info Tech volumes were -15% vs the 10-day average, and the desk was still a net seller of semis/AI.
Post-bell moves: UAL guided Q4 well below consensus (EPS $0.50-1.50 vs $1.88) with jet fuel at $4.80. COF rose 5% on a beat. ISRG fell 11% on a modest procedure beat against heightened expectations.

market_movers.rationale: Shares rose about 8% after hours on a revenue and EBITDA beat and guidance well above the Street. The desk says the market may view it as a beat vs consensus but soft vs whisper.
Fell about 5% on softer Q4 guidance and a lower 2026 ad outlook despite an EPS beat. GIR remains constructive and says Q4 guidance could prove conservative.
Rose 16% in extended trading following an earnings beat, per the opening summary.
Fell 1.7% after Q3 EPS of $2.54 vs $2.57 and a Q4 guide well below consensus, with $4.80 jet fuel.
Fell 11% on a modest procedure beat against heightened expectations, pointing to the midpoint of tightened guidance.
Shares rose over 7% after a partnership with Wolters Kluwer to integrate UpToDate into Doximity Ask.
iOS 27 WebKit changes block signals used by identity-resolution providers such as The Trade Desk, weakening open-web ad targeting.
OpenAI's acquisition of Orchestra Bio targets Veeva's core life sciences vertical. Shares dipped but ended flat.

sector_views.rationale: iOS 27 reinforces the advantage of scaled walled gardens (Meta, Google, Amazon) with logged-in first-party data, while open-web adtech faces execution risk.
Elisa missed in Q3 on competition, while Tele2's capex cut looks structural. The competitive environment is unchanged.

earnings_insights: SpaceX Q1 2027 revenue guidance is $33-37B (company guidance) vs Street about $22B (consensus estimate). Q4 capex is guided to $35-40B. The company beat revenue and EBITDA expectations, reported 10/20 after the close.
Netflix Q3 EPS beat Street and GS forecasts (reported 10/20, no figure given). Q4 growth guidance was softer and the full-year advertising outlook was reduced.

Elisa Q3 revenue was -0.2% vs consensus, MSR -2.3%, EBITDA -1.5% miss (adjusted for one-off restructuring costs), EBIT -4.9% miss, capex 14% above consensus. FY26 guidance was reiterated: telecom service revenue growth 0-2% (consensus 0.2%) and international software services organic growth 5-10% (consensus 6%).
UAL Q3 EPS was $2.54 reported vs $2.57 consensus, on revenue of $17.9bn in line with consensus. Q4 EPS was guided to $0.50-1.50 vs consensus $1.88.

Stride Q1 FY27 revenue was $639mn reported (up 3% y/y), 4% above Visible Alpha consensus, which expected a 0.8% decline. Total enrolments fell 2.5% vs consensus -0.6%. Q2 and FY27 revenue growth guidance of 1% and 2% at the midpoints matched consensus. FY27 revenue per enrolment is expected to rise 1.5-2.5% vs flat consensus.
Pearson reports Q3/9M26 on 22 October. GS expects Q3 group organic growth of 5.4% vs consensus 5.5%, and Virtual Schools growth of 9.7% vs consensus 12.4% (GS estimates).
Super Micro rose 16% in extended trading on an earnings beat. COF rose 5% on a beat. ISRG fell 11%.
Tele2 reduced 2026 capex, with only SEK50-75m slipping into 2027, about 0.2% of sales.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Slows from about +80% in 2Q and +40% in 3Q because of a higher comparison base, weaker end-market purchasing power and LTA price ceilings.

risk_factors: AI financing concerns remain, and capex is stepping up with negative FCF at SpaceX.
Power constraints are forcing idle racks at Amazon, per Business Insider.
Cloud concentration risk: a Google Cloud London outage disrupted Revolut, Lloyds and Emma.
Rising interest rates could weigh on vehicle affordability and demand, a pushback on the Auto1 data.
The impact of iOS 27 depends on adtech workarounds, adoption speed and any extension to macOS.
Elisa's FY26 guidance looks challenging given the Q3 MSR miss.
Korean tech was volatile, with a $150mn Korean neocloud IPO finishing -32% on the day.
vol_and_positioning: The US desk saw a squeezy move higher with short pockets at the top of the leaderboard. Flows were not convincing: Info Tech volumes -15% vs the 10-day average and a continued net seller of semis/AI, at a slower pace than last week.
ETF share of the tape was elevated at 32%. The floor was +3% better to buy on muted notionals.
Tele2 positioning may be somewhat short after mixed investor feedback.
geopolitical: Reports of a US-Iran proposal weighed on the US session, with QQQ recovering from a 1.1% decline.

tension_points.bull_case: SpaceX printed the cleanest AI-segment ramp yet, with SI revenue over $7.0B, payback under 1 year, a $63B backlog and raised compute capacity targets.
tension_points.bear_case: Another step-up in capex ($35-40B in Q4) and deeply negative 9M FCF, a 'spend now, monetize later' pattern. Amazon reportedly has idle racks from power constraints and multi-year FCF negativity.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Meta reporting tonight: a pure-play hyperscaler cutting 2026/27 capex under FCF pressure would test the demand case.

tension_points.bull_case: Management expects durable double-digit revenue growth from members, pricing and advertising, and GIR says Q4 guidance could prove conservative.
tension_points.bear_case: US/Canada engagement and advertising execution are the debates, with ad-product delays, third-party integrations and measurement capabilities weighing on delivery.
